constitutional-ai.d: Method by Bai et al. (Anthropic, 2022) for training a helpful, harmless assistant without human harm labels: a list of natural-language principles guides self-critique and revision (SL-CAI) and AI preference labeling (RL-CAI).

constituicao.d: A set of natural-language principles that specifies the desired behavior. In the CAI paper, 16 principles for the supervised phase and 16 for the RL phase, sampled one at a time; by 2026, Claude's document had become a long, explanatory text with an order of priorities.

sl-cai.d: The supervised phase of CAI: the model answers red team prompts, critiques its own response according to a sampled principle, revises it (4 rounds in the paper), and a pretrained model is fine-tuned with SFT on the (prompt, revision) pairs.

rl-cai.d: The reinforcement phase of CAI: a feedback model picks the less harmful of two SL-CAI responses, the soft labels train a preference model (together with human helpfulness pairs), and the policy is optimized with PPO against it.

hhh.d: Helpful, honest, harmless: the behavioral target of Anthropic's assistants. It also names an evaluation set of 221 binary comparisons.

evasividade.d: Answering sensitive requests with vague refusals (“I can't help with that”) without engaging or explaining. Human raters rewarded it in the RLHF that preceded CAI; CAI tries to replace it with responses that explain the objection.

prompt-red-team.d: A request written to provoke a harmful response and expose safety failures. The CAI paper used 42,496 written by people and 140,335 generated by few-shot prompting (182,831 in total).

critica-revisao.d: The SL-CAI loop: a critique request (point out what is harmful according to a principle) is appended to the context, followed by a revision request (rewrite without the harmful content). The first revision removes most of the harm.

destilacao-de-contexto.d: Training the model to produce, without an auxiliary context (instructions, critiques, a specification), the outputs it only produced with that context. SL-CAI and deliberative alignment strip the scaffolding from the training example.

ensemble-de-principios.d: Sampling a different principle for each revision or label, instead of always using the same one. In CAI it made the preference model more robust and increased the diversity of the revisions.

modelo-de-feedback.d: The model that labels preferences in RLAIF. In CAI, a pretrained LM that reads the conversation, a principle and options (A) and (B); the log-probabilities of the two tokens become the soft label.

modelo-de-preferencia.d: The name Anthropic uses for the reward model trained on comparisons: it gives a scalar score \( r_\phi(x,y) \) and models \( P(A \succ B) = \sigma(r_A - r_B) \). In RL-CAI, trained on 135,296 human pairs + 182,831 AI pairs.

cadeia-de-pensamento.d: Step-by-step reasoning written out before the answer. In a labeler, it improves agreement with humans, but tends to produce near-0/1 probabilities, which led CAI to clamp them.

clamp-de-rotulo.d: Clamping soft labels to a range, such as 40–60% in CAI with CoT. It limits the preference model's optimal margin (\( \mathrm{logit}(0.6) \approx 0.405 \)); without it, RL-CAI learned more extreme responses.

d-rlaif.d: A variant by Lee et al. (2023) in which an LLM gives each response a score from 1 to 10 during RL, without training a preference model. It avoids a “stale” PM and matched or beat canonical RLAIF.

proxy.d: A measure that is optimized in place of the true objective, such as a preference model standing in for human judgment. Fine while the optimization is weak; exploited when it is strong (Goodhart).

polis.d: An online deliberation platform where participants write statements and vote on other people's. It was used in Collective Constitutional AI: 1,002 US adults, 1,127 statements, 38,252 votes.

deliberative-alignment.d: OpenAI's method (Guan et al., 2024; o1/o3-mini series) that teaches the model to recall and reason about a safety specification in its CoT: SFT through context distillation (spec removed from the prompt) and RL with a judge that sees the spec, but not the CoT.

especificacao.d: A document of behavior policies, organized by category, that the model must follow. In deliberative alignment, it is the long, structured counterpart of the CAI constitution.

rule-based-rewards.d: OpenAI's method (Mu et al., 2024): rules for desired and undesired behavior evaluated by a few-shot LLM grader, used directly as the reward in RL. Safety × helpfulness F1 of 97.1 versus 91.7 for the human-feedback baseline.

constitutional-classifiers.d: Input and output classifiers (Anthropic, 2025) trained on synthetic data generated from a constitution of permitted and restricted content. They don't change the policy; they cost +0.38 percentage points of refusals and 23.7% inference overhead.

restricoes-rigidas.d: Limits that a constitution declares uncrossable, regardless of instructions or context, such as never providing serious uplift to a biological weapons attack (Claude's constitution, 2026).

autopreferencia.d: An LLM judge's tendency to favor responses from its own model or in its own style. In a self-labeling pipeline, it can reinforce the model's preferences instead of correcting them.

sobre-recusa.d: Refusing safe requests that merely sound dangerous. Measured, for example, by the refusal rate on XSTest's 250 safe prompts. It is the error opposite to undue compliance.

cumprimento-indevido.d: Fulfilling a request that should have been refused, delivering harmful content. Measured by benchmarks such as StrongREJECT and HarmBench; it is the error opposite to over-refusal.

xstest.d: An over-refusal benchmark: 250 safe prompts of 10 types, which a calibrated model shouldn't refuse, and 200 unsafe contrast prompts.

strongreject.d: An undue-compliance benchmark with prompts that require specific harmful information and an evaluator that measures the usefulness of the response; it shows that jailbreaks tend to degrade the model's capability.

harmbench.d: A standardized automated red teaming framework (18 attack methods, 33 target LLMs and defenses) that measures attack success rate with a classifier.

calibracao-de-probabilidade.d: A labeler or classifier is calibrated when its probabilities match the frequencies: of the times it says 70%, it is right about 70% of the time. That is what allows \( p_A \) to be used as a target for confidence, and not just direction; near-0/1 labels from an overconfident CoT are poorly calibrated.

bbq.d: A benchmark of social bias in questions about people from different groups, with ambiguous contexts (the right answer is “can't be determined”) and disambiguated ones; it measures how much the model falls back on stereotypes. Used in Collective Constitutional AI.
